deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page is headed Litt. R. It continues the previous page, 'Bestimmung der Elemente der Pallas aus folgenden 4 Opposit.', for the oppositions of 1803 Jun 30, 1804 Aug 30, 1805 Nov 29 and 1807 May 4. Times are in days counted from 1802 Dec 31.0: t = 181.021354, 608.209491, 1064.471030, 1585.611736. The previous page fixed the node (172°28'56.80" for 1803) and the inclination (34°37'41.55"). It also gave the true anomalies of the trial hypothesis 'Aphel. 1803 = 301°3'10.47", φ = 14°10'58.94"': v = 154°0'14.96", 212°48'34.27", 308°50'46.12", 107°49'46.05". Here φ is Gauss's eccentricity angle, e = sin φ.

This page does four things for that hypothesis: (A) converts v to E and M; (B) writes the derivatives of M with respect to the aphelion (x) and φ (y), both in arcseconds; (C) requires one constant mean motion over the three intervals and solves for x and y; (D) derives the new elements: mean motion, log a, log p, epochs of mean longitude, and a correction of i and Ω from the latitude residuals.

(A) Four columns, one per opposition.
- Row 1: log e = 9.3892022 = log sin φ.
- Row 2: log|cos v|.
- Row 3: e cos v = -0.22023, -0.20593, +0.15368, -0.07502. Gauss struck the last entry and wrote the log only.
- Row 4: log(1+e cos v) = 9.8919661, 9.8998567, 0.0620870, 9.9661316.
- Row 5: log|sin v|.
- Row 6: (1/2) log(1+e cos v).
- Row 7: log|sin v| - (1/2) log(1+e cos v).
- Row 8: log sin(φ/2) = 9.0915072.
- These give sin((v-E)/2) = sin(φ/2) sin v / sqrt(1+e cos v), which is Theoria Motus art. 8: sin½(v-E) = sin½φ sin v √(r/p).
- Results: (v-E)/2 = 3°30'47", 4°18'18", 5°8'9", 7°1'8". Hence |v-E| = 7°1'34.66", 8°36'37.025", 10°16'18.13", 14°2'16.77".
- E = 146°58'40.30", 221°25'11.295", 319°7'4.25", 93°47'29.28".
- Check on sin E: log sin E = log sin v - log(1+e cos v) + log cos φ, with log cos φ = -0.0134442 (marginal note '134442'). The rows 9.7498113 → 9.7363671 etc. carry this out.
- log e" = 4.7036273, i.e. e = 50539" in arc. Then e sin E = 27541.93" = 7°39'1.93", 33435.192" = 9°17'15.19", 33078.10" = 9°11'18.10", 50428.46" = 14°0'28.46".
- Kepler's equation M = E - e sin E gives M = 139°19'38.37", 230°42'26.49", 328°18'22.35", 79°47'0.82".

(B) Partial derivatives of M at fixed observed longitude, so that dv = -dπ.
- ∂M/∂π = -cos^3φ/(1+e cos v)^2. Here 3 log cos φ = 9.9596674 (marginal '403326'); log coefficient = 9.9596674 - 2 log(1+e cos v).
- ∂M/∂φ = -cos^2φ sin v (2+e cos v)/(1+e cos v)^2. This is computed as [x-coefficient]·(sin v/cos φ)·(2+e cos v). Rows: 9.6552216 = log(sin v/cos φ); 0.2503640 = log(2+e cos v).
- Resulting coefficients:
  - x: -1.498772, -1.445287, -0.684689, -1.065134
  - y: -1.205926, +1.449152, +1.184579, -2.013254

(C) Mean motion.
- Intervals: Δt = 427.188137, 456.261539, 521.140706 d.
- ΔM = 91°22'48.12" = 328968.12", 97°35'55.86" = 351355.86", 111°28'38.47" = 401318.47".
- Coefficient differences: (+0.053485x + 2.655078y), (+0.760598x - 0.264573y), (-0.380445x - 3.197833y).
- ΔM/Δt = 770" + remainder/Δt, with remainders 33.2545, 34.4750 (corrected from 34.2250) and 40.1264. This gives:
  - n = 770.077845 + 0.000125202x + 0.006215243y
  - n = 770.075560 + 0.001667022x - 0.000579871y
  - n = 770.076998 - 0.000730024x - 0.006136218y
- Differences, in units of 0.001":
  - -2.285 + 1.541820x - 6.795114y = 0
  - +1.438 - 2.397046x - 5.556347y = 0
  - Gauss struck the earlier constants 3.305 and 2.458.
- Normalised: x - 4.4073y = 1.4820 and x + 2.3180y = 0.5999. Hence 6.7253y = -0.8821 (logs 9.94552 - 0.82771 = 9.11781).
- Result: y = -0.13", x = +0.90".
- New elements: aphelion 1803 = 301°3'11.37"; φ = 14°10'58.81"; log e = 9.3892011; e = 0.2450198.
- Sidereal n ≈ 770.07714"/d (all three equations agree). Tropical n = sidereal + 0.137166" = 50.1"/365.25 (Gauss writes 'Trop.'); about 770.2143".
- Kepler III with log k = 3.5500066 (k = 3548.18761"):
  - log a = (2/3)(3.5500066 - 2.8865342) = 0.4423149, so a ≈ 2.7685.
  - log p = log a + 2 log cos φ = 0.4423149 - 0.0268882 = 0.4154268.
- log(1+e cos v) and log cos v were recomputed with the new elements (9.8919667, ...; 9.3892011, 9.9536746, ...).

(D) Epochs.
- Corrected mean anomalies:
  - M1 = 139°19'38.37" - 1.498772(0.90) - 1.205926(-0.13) = 139°19'37.18"
  - M4 = 79°47'0.12"
- Add the perihelion of date: 121°3'36.70" (1803) and 121°6'49.38" (1807). They differ by 192.7", about 1404 d of precession.
- Mean longitudes: L = 260°23'13.89" and 200°53'49.50".
- Reduce to 0h of the day:
  - 0.021354 d × n: log 8.3294792 + 2.8866115 → 16.45"
  - 0.611736 d × n: log 9.7865641 + 2.8866115 → 7'51.17"
- Results: L(1803 day 181.0) = 260°22'57.44"; L(1807 day 1585.0) = 200°45'58.76" (or .33).
- Motion table at tropical n = 770.21433":
  - 1404 d = 300°23'0.92"
  - 108 d = 23°6'23.148"
  - 12 d = 2°34'2.572"
  - 4 d = 51'20.857"
  - 1 d = 12'50.214"
  - 1416 d = 302°57'3.49"
  - 177 d = 37°52'7.94"
  - 181 d = 38°43'28.79"
  - 124 d = 26°31'46.58"
  - 185 d = 39°34'49.65"
- Hence the epoch table of mean longitude, 1802-1809: 143°34'0.42", 221°39'28.65" (= 260°22'57.44" - 38°43'28.79"), 299°57'47.09", 18°3'15.32", 96°8'43.55", 174°14'11.78", 252°32'30.22", 330°37'58.45".
- Successive differences are 365·n or 366·n. The 366-day steps fall at 1803→1804 and 1807→1808. This is the usual table convention: epoch Jan 0 in common years, Jan 1 in leap years.
- Aphelion of date: 1807 301°6'31.77" and 1808 301°7'21.97", i.e. +50.1"/yr from 1803.0.

(D') Latitudes and the i, Ω correction.
- Columns of logs and angles reduce the observed geocentric latitudes (46°26'36.00", 15°1'49.80", -54°30'54.93", 42°11'25.60") to heliocentric ones: 33°41'24.13", 10°27'8.16", -33°40'30.08", 28°15'7.08".
- Comparison with the orbit values of the previous page gives the 'Errores latt. heli.' +20.13, +4.23, -29.21, +10.26.
- 'Hinc correctio': δi = -0.52", δΩ = +0.06". This is evidently a least-squares (normal-equation) solution with dβ = (sin(λ-Ω) cos²β/cos²i) di - tan i cos(λ-Ω) cos²β dΩ. My recomputation gives δi ≈ -0.48" and |δΩ| ≈ 0.06", provided the 1804 residual is taken as -4.23 in signed latitude.
errors: No substantive computational errors were found. The checked logarithms, conversions to E and M, differences, quotients and the 2x2 elimination all agree to the last place or within 1-2 units of the 7th decimal.

Gauss himself corrected a slip in interval 2: the remainder was first 34.2250", then 34.4750", giving n = 770.075560. This forced the replacement of the constants 3.305 and 2.458 by 2.285 and 1.438, and of -0.000464664 by -0.000730024.
The normalised coefficient 4.4073 is 4.40720 exactly (6.795114/1.541820). The difference is negligible for y = -0.13.

200°53'49.50" - 7'51.17" = 200°45'58.33", whereas the page appears to read 58.76 (possibly overwritten). With 58.33 the 1807 epoch 174°14'11.75" agrees with the tabular 174°14'11.78"; with 58.76 there is a 0.4" discrepancy.

Sign convention of the latitude residuals is inconsistent with the previous-page values. 1804: obs 10°27'8.16" vs calc 10°27'12.39" would be -4.23, but +4.23 is written; 1805 (south latitude) is written -29.21. The least-squares result δi ≈ -0.5" is reproduced only if the 1804 residual is effectively -4.23 in signed latitude. So either the written sign is a slip or the convention differs.

The perihelion of date 121°3'36.70" exceeds 121°3'11.37" by 25.33", slightly more than the 181 d × 0.137166 = 24.83" of precession. The extra ~0.5" (also present in 1807) is unexplained, perhaps nutation; unsure.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working sheet of Gauss's well-documented 1807 Pallas orbit determination from four oppositions. It uses the Theoria Motus anomaly formulas, differential corrections, the Gaussian constant and a least-squares fit for i and Ω. All of this is known to be his, and the Pallas oppositions are the published Theoria Motus least-squares example. The interest is only as a detailed unpublished computation record.
